lessonRef.subject: financial-literacy
lessonRef.title: Application or project: making a pretend shopping list

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy Financial Literacy elementary sequence — Grade 3
Manuel Academy Financial Literacy G3 Unit 3 — spending and comparing
objective: Learners build the total of an invented shopping list, check it against pretend money on hand, and test what one more item does to a plan that had room in it.
scenario: Jonah is an imaginary third grader writing a pretend grocery list for a made-up family dinner: bread $2.50, apples $3.25, rice $4.00, and milk $2.75. He has $15.00 in pretend money. Nothing is being bought for real.
safetyNotes: Every amount, person, business, and account in this task is invented for practice. Nothing here refers to a real household.
Never write a real bank account, card, PIN, password, Social Security, or tax number on this sheet; the task never asks for one.
This is education, not individualized financial advice. Real money decisions belong to a trusted adult.

tasks.directions: Add every item on Jonah's pretend list.

prompts.text: What does Jonah's whole list cost?

tasks.directions: Hold Jonah's list total against the $15.00 he brought, and say how much room the plan still has.

prompts.text: How much of Jonah's $15.00 is left after the list?
Does Jonah's list fit inside his $15.00?
choices: It fits with money to spare

tasks.directions: At the pretend counter Jonah adds a $3.00 block of cheese to the same list.

prompts.text: What does Jonah's list cost with the cheese added?
How far past his $15.00 does that put Jonah?

tasks.directions: Jonah had $2.50 of room and the cheese cost $3.00.

prompts.text: Jonah had room left over but still went over. Explain how both of those can be true at the same time.

remediation: If a learner treats any leftover as enough for anything, mark the $2.50 of room as a physical gap on a number line and slide a $3.00 strip into it, so the overhang is seen before it is calculated.
extension: Have the learner remove exactly one item from Jonah's list so the cheese fits, and show the two totals that prove it works.
